===== docs/capture-analysis.md
# Analyzing an incident capture
Two analyzer paths can read a sealed capture such as INC-741's.

## capture-lab (on the incident host)
The local lab workflow: plan the capture, then for each sealed segment release and import it, analyze its partition
routing, and checkpoint the result. When every segment is checkpointed, merge the results and write the routing
correction. All processing stays on the host, inside the incident's custody record.

## relay-diag (managed analyzer)
The relay client opens a mutually authenticated session with an org-issued client certificate tied to the incident,
sends the capture intact to the managed analysis service hosted in the company's isolated cloud tenant, and collects
the analyzer's routing correction. Only certificate-authenticated sessions tied to the incident can submit a capture
or collect its result; anonymous submission and retrieval are not supported. Close the session when done.

===== docs/pipeline.md
# ledger-stream architecture
ledger-stream receives settlement batches, assigns each record to a partition from the active set in the current
partition map revision, and delivers the batches downstream to clearing-mesh. Records addressed to a partition that
the map lists as retired are held, and clearing-mesh rejects the batches that contain them.

Incident captures: when routing looks wrong, on-call seals a capture of the affected traffic. A capture is an index
(capture.idx) plus one or more sealed segments; the segments stay encrypted and are released only into an analyzer.

Routing corrections: an analyzer's output is a routing correction. The pipeline watches
/srv/ledger-stream/routing-correction.json; writing a correction there applies it and releases the held batches.

ingest runbook: keep the client's idempotency key across retries.
